$comment: Copy to your project root as flow.config.json. EVERY key is optional: what you omit is autodetected. This file always wins over autodetection. `subproject` (below) is monorepo-only: set when `rein detect` reports stack:'monorepo' -- the kit never guesses which sub-project is the target (a wrong guess is worse than asking), so this is the ONLY way any command resolves at all.

commands.$comment: {target} is substituted with a single test file or test id. Bounded verification is the point: never the whole suite inside an implementation step. `serve` (frontend subtypes only) is how to start the dev server for rendered verification -- set it whenever the server isn't an npm `dev`/`start` script (static site, a Django/Rails-served front end, docker compose); it always wins over the package.json script lookup.

plan.$comment: openspec = openspec/changes/<change>/{proposal,design,tasks,specs}. tasks-md = a plain tasks.md with checkboxes.

tracker.$comment: none = tasks.md checkboxes are the state. beads = also sync/close Beads issues (requires the bd CLI).

ship.$comment: rein ship tuning (all optional; these are the defaults). claudeWeeklyThreshold: Claude weekly usage % above which workers go to Codex. maxConcurrentWorkers: live workers at once. maxRetries: fresh retries of a red task. maxAuditRounds: fix-and-reaudit rounds before escalating. taskTimeoutMinutes: wall time per task before a gate opens. largeChangeFiles: changed-file count that routes the audit to Opus. riskyPaths: globs that also route the audit to Opus.

retrieval.$comment: auto = use codegraph if an index exists, otherwise plain search. Presence is probed; a missing tool degrades the flow, never breaks it.

verify.$comment: mode: 'auto' (default) detects from the stack -- frontend subtypes get 'rendered', infra without a test command gets 'plan-only', everything else gets 'unit'. Set explicitly to override: 'rendered' requires a real observed browser render (Playwright / Claude-in-Chrome) instead of a passing test suite alone -- 'the tests pass but the UI is broken' is the failure this catches. 'plan-only' forbids destructive ops against real infrastructure. 'unit' is today's plain test-suite behavior. Asking for MORE than detection inferred needs nothing; asking for LESS ('unit' where 'rendered' or 'plan-only' was detected) needs "until": "YYYY-MM-DD" and stops applying after that date -- an exception without an expiry is not an exception, it is the new default. url overrides the auto-detected dev-server URL used for rendered checks (e.g. when the app is served under a subpath).
